summary: Groenendijk & Stokhof 1991 Dynamic Predicate Logic: the semantics as a relation between total assignments, factored through eight relation operators so that Def. 2's set-builder clauses hold literally; truth, validity, tests and conditions; Facts 1-6 of sec. 3.2 with the converse of Fact 6 refuted; variable-level binding (AQV/FV), Fact 9 and the transfer lemma underlying the source's inductions; the displayed laws of sec. 3.4 including Egli's Theorem and Corollary, with the printed idempotency-of-disjunction law refuted (d34_refuted); the sec. 3.5 entailment notions (Facts 10-16) with the source's separating examples; the three donkey sentences with their relational meanings and first-order truth conditions, and equiv dk2 dk3 via Egli's Corollary.

sources.citation: Groenendijk, J. & Stokhof, M. (1991). Dynamic Predicate Logic. Linguistics and Philosophy 14(1):39-100.
Dekker, P. (2012). Dynamic Semantics. Springer. Sec. 2.1.

evidence: sem unfolds to Def. 2's set-builder clauses literally via the eight relation operators.
The audit block's three groups printed exactly as documented: 18 theorems axiom-free, 9 with classic only, 6 with functional_extensionality_dep.
Fact 6's printed converse and the printed idempotency-of-disjunction law (phi ~ phi \/ phi) are refuted by countermodel (fact6_refuted, d34_refuted), with what does hold proved alongside.
The donkey sentences' first-order truth conditions are proved as biconditionals over an arbitrary domain.
simplifications: variable-level binding only (occurrence-level Defs 13-14 and Fact 7 omitted, following the source's own caveat)
closure as formula-level double negation (licensed by D19)
omissions: D50 (alphabetic variants) — needs a DPL-aware substitution operator and the printed side condition is insufficient
additions: the transfer lemma and its given-output variant as the reusable induction behind Facts 8, 13-16 and the conditional laws
explicit refutations d34_refuted, fact6_refuted with countermodels over a two-element domain

determination_rationale: The relational semantics, laws and entailment notions go through as in the source; classical logic is needed exactly where the source reasons classically (9 theorems), and functional extensionality only for results that pin down a prescribed output assignment (6 theorems). Two printed claims of the source are false as stated and are refuted with countermodels, with corrected forms proved.

artifact_classes.description: meanings are relations between total assignments (predicates on pairs); satisfaction/production sets are predicates, not sets
no finite-set library: variable sets as predicates/lists with hand-rolled agreement lemmas
classic for the source's classical reasoning (9 theorems); functional_extensionality_dep for given-output transfer results (6 theorems); both isolated and documented per theorem

source_gap.detail: G&S 1991 print phi ~ phi \/ phi among the sec. 3.4 laws — refuted (d34_refuted); the converse direction of Fact 6 is also false as printed — refuted (fact6_refuted). Def. 12 (conditions) omits the universal clause restored here. Recorded in the file's SOURCE NOTES.
